title: Point CANONICAL_PI_SCOPE at the new npm scope and widen PI_SCOPE_ALIASES (must land with the W7 scope rename, not before it)
wave: Wave 1 (M5 §6.1) — as written. RECOMMENDED: split into W2a (wave 1, shippable alone) and W2b (ships with or immediately after W7 pass 1).
one_line: Add `ultraworkers` to the list of npm scopes the extension loader accepts and repoint the canonical scope string at `@ultraworkers`, so a plugin that imports `@ultraworkers/pi-utils` is served the exact copy of the package already running inside the host instead of a second copy pulled from npm.
user_visible_effect: After W2b: an extension declaring `@ultraworkers/pi-*` in peerDependencies loads against the host's in-process copy — same module registry, same tool registry — instead of linking a duplicate (and, for pi-natives, a second copy of the native addon). If W2b were to land WITHOUT the W7 manifest rename, the opposite happens and it is worse: every `@oh-my-pi/*` import stops going through the canonicalizer, so extensions silently start carrying duplicate native modules again.
effort: S — two string edits in one file, plus two cases appended to an existing test file. The verification work is the bulk of it: `bun test` is blocked in this environment until the native addon is built.
depends_on: W1 (soft, cosmetic: keeps the diff free of wire-literal churn; W2's two lines are in a different file from W1's five, so this is ordering hygiene rather than a real dependency)
For W2b ONLY: W7 pass 1 must have landed, because W7 is what makes the `@ultraworkers` scope actually exist on disk. This is the load-bearing dependency and the plan does not state it correctly.
blocks: W7 (the plan declares W2 a hard prerequisite of W7; see plan_corrections — the real relationship is that W2 and W7 pass 1 must not be separated by a release, and W2's alias-only half is what genuinely must precede W7)

steps.instruction: W2a — append `"ultraworkers"` as the FIRST element of `PI_SCOPE_ALIASES`, giving `const PI_SCOPE_ALIASES = ["ultraworkers", "oh-my-pi", "mariozechner", "earendil-works"] as const;`. Keep `CANONICAL_PI_SCOPE` at line 796 exactly as it is (`"@oh-my-pi"`). Do NOT touch line 805 or line 808. Do NOT reformat the surrounding comment block (lines 789-795 and 798-801) beyond the minimum needed to stay truthful — the comment at 789-795 says 'or the canonical @oh-my-pi scope itself', which is still true at this point because the canonical scope is still @oh-my-pi; the comment at 798-801 explains why `@oh-my-pi` stays in the list forever, and that reason is unchanged.

W2a adds NO test case. Reason: at this point `@ultraworkers/pi-utils` does not exist on disk (the 16 manifests still read `@oh-my-pi/...`), so the canonical-path column of the test harness — which is built from `Bun.resolveSync` at module scope, lines 24-34 — has nothing to resolve it to. A case added now would either throw at import time or assert nothing. The new cases belong to W2b.

W2b (only after W7 pass 1 has merged and `bun install` has been re-run) — change `const CANONICAL_PI_SCOPE = "@oh-my-pi";` to `const CANONICAL_PI_SCOPE = "@ultraworkers";`. This one line is the entire substance of W2b; line 802 was already done in W2a. Do NOT touch line 805 or line 808 — those are host-bundled package basenames, a separate product decision settled at N17 (keep all 16 basenames unchanged). Do NOT add the 10 other published basenames (`pi-catalog`, `pi-metaharness`, `pi-mnemopi`, `pi-wire`, `omp-stats`, `omptype`, `snapcompact`, `browser-relay`, `collab-web`, `typescript-edit-benchmark`) to `PI_PACKAGE_NAMES`; they are out of W2's scope and adding them is N17's decision, not this work item's.

W2b — append to `CASES` a case `{ id: "ultraworkers-utils", aliasSpecifier: "@ultraworkers/pi-utils", canonicalPath: canonicalUtils, symbol: "logger" }`. `canonicalUtils` already exists at line 29. The harness at lines 109-117 then generates the identity assertion for free: the plugin imports `logger` from `@ultraworkers/pi-utils` and from the absolute canonical path, and throws unless the two bindings are `===`. That single assertion is the whole contract: same-scope and new-scope imports land on ONE instance, not two npm copies.

W2b — the second case the plan asks for (a plugin DECLARING `@ultraworkers` in `peerDependencies` still resolves) is best expressed inside the same generated probe rather than as a new file: add a `peerDependencies` field to the probe plugin's `package.json` object at line 96-100 listing every alias scope under test (`{"@oh-my-pi/pi-utils": "*", "@ultraworkers/pi-utils": "*", "@mariozechner/pi-utils": "*"}`). Nothing in the loader reads that field for resolution — it is declared, never installed, and the extension still loads. That is the point: resolution must come from the host's canonicalizer, not from a locally installed peer. If a future regression made the loader start honouring plugin-local node_modules, the identity assertion in step 4 is what would catch it.

Run the audit greps from the verification block, and specifically confirm the two guard invariants before committing: (a) `git grep -n '"oh-my-pi"' -- packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/plugins/legacy-pi-compat.ts` still returns line 802 — the old scope must remain in the alias list forever (N8); (b) `git diff` touches exactly two lines of source and does not touch line 805. Both are cheap and both catch the single most damaging mistake in this work item.

Before calling W2b done, hand-verify the compiled-binary path, which no in-process test can reach. The bundled registry keys come from `manifest.name` (`packages/coding-agent/scripts/legacy-pi-virtual-module.ts:126`), and `loadBundledModule` throws `omp:legacy-pi-shim: no bundled module registered for <key>` at line 752-754 when a key is absent. So after W2b, a build made WITHOUT the W7 manifest rename produces a binary whose registry is keyed `@oh-my-pi/pi-ai` while `LEGACY_PI_AI_SHIM_PATH` asks for `@ultraworkers/pi-ai` — every bundled extension load dies. Confirm by inspection that the manifest rename from W7 is present in the same branch as the W2b commit (`git grep -m1 '"name"' packages/utils/package.json` returns `@ultraworkers/pi-utils`). This is the check that catches the W2b-without-W7 ordering bug, and it works even though `bun test` is blocked.

test_contract:
DEFENDED CONTRACT: a plugin that imports a host-bundled `pi-*` package through ANY accepted npm scope — `@ultraworkers`, `@oh-my-pi`, `@mariozechner`, or `@earendil-works` — receives the SAME module instance the host itself is running, not a per-plugin npm copy. The test proves this by object identity (`alias !== canonical` throws inside the generated plugin), never by string comparison against a constant, so it cannot pass vacuously.

WHAT A CONSUMER SEES IF IT REGRESSES: (1) a plugin declares `@ultraworkers/pi-utils` in peerDependencies and the host serves it a private second copy — a second module registry and a second tool registry, so a tool registered by the host is invisible to the plugin, and `pi-natives` gets linked twice, doubling the native addon in the user's tree; (2) the mirror-image failure if the alias list loses `oh-my-pi`: every existing extension written against the old scope dies at plugin-load time with module-not-found — a runtime error, not a build error, so nothing in CI catches it until a user tries to load a real plugin. Both failure modes are covered by the same identity assertion; the second is additionally covered by the surviving `@oh-my-pi` cases already in the file (lines 53, 55-59).

NOT defended here, and deliberately so: the 10 published basenames outside `PI_PACKAGE_NAMES` (`pi-catalog`, `pi-metaharness`, `pi-mnemopi`, `pi-wire`, `omp-stats`, `omptype`, `snapcompact`, `browser-relay`, `collab-web`, `typescript-edit-benchmark`). They do not match `LEGACY_PI_SPECIFIER_FILTER` and were never canonicalized at HEAD either. Asserting anything about them would be a new product decision, which is N17's job.

gate:
W2a gate (wave 1, runs today): `bun run check:ts` exits 0, and `git grep -n '"@oh-my-pi"' -- packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/plugins/legacy-pi-compat.ts` still reports line 802. W2a deliberately ships with no new test case, so the greps ARE its gate — they are the only thing that distinguishes a correct W2a from a W2a that accidentally also flipped the canonical scope.

W2b gate (after W7): `cd packages/coding-agent && bun test test/pi-scope-aliases.test.ts` reports 1 pass / 0 fail (requires the native addon), AND `git grep -m1 '"name"' -- packages/utils/package.json` prints `@ultraworkers/pi-utils`. Both are required: the first proves the identity contract, the second proves the compiled-binary registry will have the keys the canonicalizer now asks for.

CAN THE GATE GO RED? For W2b, yes, in two independent ways. (1) If the canonical scope were flipped but the alias list lost `@oh-my-pi`, the existing cases at test lines 53 and 55-59 load plugins that import `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils` and `@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent`; those imports stop resolving and `result.errors` is non-empty, so line 131 `expect(result.errors).toEqual([])` fails. (2) If W2b landed before W7, `Bun.resolveSync("@ultraworkers/pi-utils")` throws at test-module scope, so the file fails to even evaluate and the run reports 0 pass / 1 fail — a red gate, not a green one. For W2a the gate is weaker by design: with no new test case, the only failure it can catch is the dropped `"@oh-my-pi"` alias, and only because the grep is written to look for it.
risk:
The single most likely way to get this wrong is shipping W2b before W7, and it is worse than the plan's own stated risk. The plan's stated worst case is that running the W7 sed first leaves the canonicalizer pointing at the old scope, so extensions silently link a duplicate native module. The actual failure of doing it in the plan's order is HARDER, not softer, and it has two separate mechanisms that I verified rather than inferred:

(1) Dev / source mode. `remapLegacyPiSpecifier` (:1057-1069) rewrites every accepted scope to `${CANONICAL_PI_SCOPE}/...`, so `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils` becomes `@ultraworkers/pi-utils`. `getResolvedSpecifier` (:1077) calls `Bun.resolveSync`, which throws — I ran it: `Cannot find module '@ultraworkers/pi-utils'`. The `try/catch` at :1144-1149 swallows the throw, so the shim is bypassed and old-scope plugins keep working only by accident, via Bun resolving `@oh-my-pi/*` from the workspace root. Net effect: the canonicalizer is silently dead, which is the same duplicate-native-module harm the plan describes, just arriving by the opposite route.

(2) Compiled binary / `PI_BUNDLED=1`. `LEGACY_PI_AI_SHIM_PATH` (:951-953) becomes `omp-legacy-pi-bundled:@ultraworkers/pi-ai`, but the registry is keyed by `manifest.name` (`packages/coding-agent/scripts/legacy-pi-virtual-module.ts:126`), still `@oh-my-pi/pi-ai`. `loadBundledModule` (:752-754) throws `omp:legacy-pi-shim: no bundled module registered for @ultraworkers/pi-ai`. That is a hard crash on every bundled extension load, and no in-process test can reach it — which is why step 7 is an inspection check rather than a test.

(3) The plan's OWN acceptance test cannot pass before W7. It says a plugin importing `@ultraworkers/pi-utils` and one importing `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils` must canonicalize to the same specifier. The `@ultraworkers` one hard-fails with module-not-found until the manifests are renamed, so the prescribed command `bun test test/extension-scope-canonicalization.test.ts` goes red on a correct-looking W2a.

Second-order risk, nearly as likely: creating the new test file the plan names. `test/pi-scope-aliases.test.ts` already exists and already asserts the identical contract by object identity. A second file doing the same thing is the duplicate-coverage pattern AGENTS.md bans, and it will drift.

Third: 'helpfully' adding the 10 missing basenames to `PI_PACKAGE_NAMES` while you are in the file. It looks like finishing the job and it is a different product decision (N17) with a much larger blast radius.
open_questions: Do we accept the W2a / W2b split, or does the milestone owner want W2 kept as one commit that must be merged in the same PR as W7 pass 1? The split is strictly safer (it creates no window in which the canonical scope names a scope that does not exist) but it does move one line of W2 out of wave 1, which is a visible change to the plan's wave structure. A human must decide because it reorders the milestone, not just the code.

If W2b and W7 pass 1 must ship together, who owns the release gate that stops W2b from being cherry-picked alone? A CODEOWNERS entry or a CI check asserting `git grep -m1 '"name"' -- packages/utils/package.json` returns `@ultraworkers/pi-utils` whenever `CANONICAL_PI_SCOPE` is `@ultraworkers` would make the failure impossible rather than merely documented.

N17 is recorded as settled ('keep all 16 basenames') but the plan's own open-questions table still presents it as an open product decision. W2 must not resolve it either way. Confirm the plan's final position before anyone touches `PI_PACKAGE_NAMES`.

plan_corrections.claim: W2 can ship on its own in wave 1, as a separate commit, BEFORE W7. ('Phải là một commit riêng, trước W7' — plan:8677; 'Effort: S — 2 sửa chuỗi cộng một test' — plan:8681.)
plan_corrections.correction: W2 as a single commit cannot ship before W7. Setting `CANONICAL_PI_SCOPE = "@ultraworkers"` before the 16 manifests are renamed points the canonicalizer at a scope that does not exist: in dev mode every remap throws and the throw is swallowed at :1144-1149, and in a compiled binary every bundled extension load dies at :752-754. Split it: W2a (wave 1) adds `"ultraworkers"` to `PI_SCOPE_ALIASES` only and is genuinely shippable alone; W2b flips `CANONICAL_PI_SCOPE` and ships with or immediately after W7. W2a on its own is a no-op today (the scope does not exist yet) and already correct the moment W7 lands, so no commit in the history ever aims the canonicalizer at a missing scope. Note this also violates the plan's own structural requirement at line 8650 that every wave be independently shippable.
plan_corrections.evidence: `bun -e 'Bun.resolveSync("@ultraworkers/pi-utils", process.cwd())'` → `Cannot find module '@ultraworkers/pi-utils' from '/Users/tranquangdang21/Projects/ultraworkers'`, while the same call for `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils` → `/Users/.../packages/utils/src/index.ts`. Source: `legacy-pi-compat.ts:1077` (`Bun.resolveSync` in `getResolvedSpecifier`), `:1144-1149` (the swallowing try/catch), `:751-754` (`loadBundledModule` throws on an unregistered key), and `packages/coding-agent/scripts/legacy-pi-virtual-module.ts:126` (`addEntry(manifest.name, ...)` — registry keys are the literal manifest name, still `@oh-my-pi/pi-ai`). A full simulation of the post-W2 filter/remap/resolve chain confirmed all four scope spellings now remap to an unresolvable `@ultraworkers/*` target.

plan_corrections.correction: An equivalent test already exists: `packages/coding-agent/test/pi-scope-aliases.test.ts` (135 lines). It builds a probe plugin importing each aliased scope alongside the `Bun.resolveSync` absolute path and throws unless the two bindings are object-identical (lines 109-117) — which is exactly the equivalence assertion the plan asks the new file to make, and it already covers `@oh-my-pi` (lines 53, 55-59) and `@mariozechner` (lines 61-66). Add the `@ultraworkers` case to its `CASES` array. Creating the named file would duplicate coverage at a second level, which AGENTS.md explicitly bans, and the two would drift.

plan_corrections.claim: W2's second test case: 'a plugin declaring `@ultraworkers` in `peerDependencies` still resolves' (plan:8682).
plan_corrections.correction: The loader never reads a plugin's `peerDependencies` to decide resolution — `isBareExtensionDependencySpecifier` (:1453-1466) only classifies the specifier shape, and `resolveExtensionBareDependency` looks in the PLUGIN's own node_modules, which by construction will not contain a peer. So the declaration is inert, and the case is only meaningful as a negative: it proves resolution came from the host canonicalizer rather than from a locally installed peer. Express it as a `peerDependencies` field on the probe plugin's `package.json` in the existing harness, not as a separate file or a separate loader path. It must be added in W2b, not W2a, because `Bun.resolveSync('@ultraworkers/pi-utils')` cannot produce the canonical-path column before W7.
plan_corrections.evidence: `legacy-pi-compat.ts:1453-1466` (`isBareExtensionDependencySpecifier` — pure shape classification, no manifest read); `:1158-1161` (the bare-dep fallback is only reached AFTER the canonicalizer has already failed, and operates on the original specifier). Simulation confirms `isBareExtensionDependencySpecifier('@ultraworkers/pi-utils')` returns true.

plan_corrections.claim: W2 must precede W7 because the two scope strings are what the W7 sed 'does not reach', so the compatibility mechanism has to be in place first (plan:8781, plan:8784 'W2 (cứng)').
plan_corrections.correction: The mechanism claim is right but the sed-clobbering reasoning is not the operative one, and conflating the two leads to the wrong ordering. The W7 pattern is `@oh-my-pi/` WITH a trailing slash; neither `"@oh-my-pi"` (:796) nor `"oh-my-pi"` (:802) contains a trailing slash, so the sed provably cannot touch either line — which is exactly what the plan itself says at 8503 and 8964. The real constraint is a RESOLVABILITY constraint: W2b is only legal once the `@ultraworkers` scope exists, i.e. after W7's manifest pass. The genuinely order-dependent piece is W2a: the alias-table widening is what keeps old-scope plugins canonicalizing across the W7 rename, and that half does belong before W7. Splitting the item separates the one real ordering constraint from the one that is only a sed-hygiene concern.
plan_corrections.evidence: `git grep -n 'CANONICAL_PI_SCOPE\|PI_SCOPE_ALIASES'` at HEAD: only `legacy-pi-compat.ts:796,802` in source — both bare-quoted, no trailing slash. Plan line 8503 and line 8964 both state the sed pattern is trailing-slash and that the bare form needs its own grep.

plan_corrections.claim: `PI_PACKAGE_NAMES` (:805) holds the package list the canonicalizer serves, so adding `ultraworkers` to the scope implies the list should track the new scope (implicit reading of the parenthetical at plan:8678).
plan_corrections.correction: `PI_PACKAGE_NAMES` is a BASENAME list of host-bundled packages and is deliberately decoupled from the scope list. It holds 6 entries while the repo publishes 16 scoped packages, so 10 published basenames — `pi-catalog`, `pi-metaharness`, `pi-mnemopi`, `pi-wire`, `omp-stats`, `omptype`, `snapcompact`, `browser-relay`, `collab-web`, `typescript-edit-benchmark` — have never matched `LEGACY_PI_SPECIFIER_FILTER` and are not canonicalized today. W2 does not change that, and this spec's tests deliberately assert nothing about them so the decision stays where N17 put it. Say this in the PR description, because the mismatch (6 vs 16) is exactly what invites a well-meaning 'fix' during review.
plan_corrections.evidence: `legacy-pi-compat.ts:805` lists exactly 6 `pi-*` basenames; `for f in packages/*/package.json; do grep -m1 '"name"' ...; done` returns exactly 16 scoped package names. A simulation confirms `@ultraworkers/omp-stats` does NOT match the post-W2 filter.
